q: An insurance company receives thousands of scanned claim forms daily. It needs to extract policy numbers and claim amounts, and route any extraction with low confidence to employees for verification. Which combination of AWS services meets these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
o: Amazon Textract and Amazon Augmented AI (A2I)
Amazon Rekognition and SageMaker Ground Truth
Amazon Comprehend and Amazon Mechanical Turk
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and Amazon Kendra
x: Textract extracts key-value pairs from forms, and A2I has a built-in Textract integration that sends low-confidence results to human reviewers. Rekognition targets photos, not forms. Ground Truth labels training data rather than reviewing live predictions.

q: A travel company built a chatbot on Amazon Bedrock. Answers about current visa rules are often outdated because the model's training data is old. The rules change monthly. Which solution will keep answers current with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Store the visa documents in Amazon S3 and connect them to an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base
Fine-tune the model every month with the new rules
Continue pre-training the model monthly on travel websites
x: RAG through Knowledge Bases retrieves the latest documents at query time. Re-syncing S3 is all that's needed when rules change. Monthly fine-tuning or continued pre-training is costly and slow, and temperature doesn't add knowledge.

q: A company wants its LLM-based support assistant to answer in exactly the company's tone and to produce a fixed JSON structure for every response. The company has 5,000 high-quality examples of prompts and ideal responses. Prompt engineering alone has produced inconsistent results. What should the company do?
o: Fine-tune a foundation model in Amazon Bedrock with the labeled prompt-response pairs
Create a knowledge base from the 5,000 examples
Use continued pre-training with unlabeled support tickets
Lower the Top K value to 1
x: Consistent style and format learned from labeled input-output pairs is the classic case for supervised fine-tuning. A knowledge base adds facts, not behavior. Continued pre-training uses unlabeled data to add domain knowledge.

q: A pharmaceutical company has 50 GB of unlabeled internal research papers. Its foundation model performs poorly because it does not understand the company's specialized chemical terminology. Which customization approach is MOST appropriate?
o: Continued pre-training on the unlabeled research papers
Few-shot prompting with three example papers
x: Large volumes of UNLABELED domain text that teach vocabulary and knowledge fit continued pre-training. Supervised fine-tuning requires labeled pairs, and few-shot examples can't teach a whole domain.

q: A startup wants to add a generative AI summarization feature. Traffic is low and unpredictable during the first months, and the company wants to avoid any upfront commitment. Which Amazon Bedrock pricing option should it choose?
x: On-Demand charges per input and output token with no commitment, which fits low, unpredictable traffic. Provisioned Throughput is for steady high volume or custom models. Reserved Instances don't apply to Bedrock.

q: A retailer must generate product descriptions for 800,000 catalog items. The job runs once and results are needed within a few days. Which approach is MOST cost-effective?
o: Submit the prompts as an Amazon Bedrock batch inference job from Amazon S3
Call the Bedrock On-Demand API in a loop from an EC2 instance
Fine-tune a model for each product category
x: Batch inference processes large prompt files asynchronously from S3 at a lower price than on-demand, which is ideal for one-time, non-urgent bulk jobs.

q: A bank's virtual assistant uses an FM on Amazon Bedrock. Regulators require that the assistant never gives investment recommendations and never reveals customers' account numbers in responses. Which solution meets both requirements?
o: Configure Amazon Bedrock Guardrails with a denied topic for investment advice and a sensitive information filter for account numbers
Use Amazon Macie to scan the chatbot's responses
Add 'do not give investment advice' to the user prompt
Use SageMaker Clarify to detect investment advice
x: Guardrails denied topics block a subject area and sensitive information filters mask or block PII patterns, for both prompts and responses. Macie scans S3, not live responses. A prompt instruction alone is not a reliable control.

q: An e-commerce company wants an assistant that can look up a customer's order in its order database, check refund eligibility using company policy documents, and then issue the refund through an internal API. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: An Amazon Bedrock agent with an action group for the order and refund APIs and a knowledge base for policy documents
An Amazon Bedrock knowledge base only
x: Multi-step reasoning plus API actions plus document lookup is exactly what Agents do: action groups call APIs and the attached knowledge base supplies policy context. A knowledge base alone cannot take actions.

q: A company needs to choose between three foundation models for summarizing legal contracts. It wants to compare them on its own sample contracts using automated metrics and also have its legal team rate the summaries. Which solution requires the LEAST effort?
o: Use Amazon Bedrock model evaluation with automatic and human-based evaluation jobs
Deploy all three models to SageMaker endpoints and build a custom scoring app
Use SageMaker Model Monitor on all three models
x: Bedrock model evaluation supports custom prompt datasets, automatic metrics, and human evaluation with your own work team, with nothing to build.

q: A hospital wants to transcribe doctor-patient conversations and then automatically extract medications and diagnoses from the transcripts. Which services should it use?
o: Amazon Transcribe Medical and Amazon Comprehend Medical
x: Transcribe Medical converts clinical speech to text, and Comprehend Medical extracts medical entities such as medications, conditions and dosages. Both are HIPAA eligible.

q: A media company receives millions of user-uploaded photos each day. It must automatically block images containing explicit or violent content and send borderline cases to human moderators. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: Amazon Rekognition content moderation with Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) for human review
x: Rekognition's moderation API detects unsafe image content with confidence scores, and A2I routes low-confidence results to human moderators. Guardrails word filters work on text, not images.

q: A global company's employees ask HR and IT questions all day. The answers are in SharePoint and Confluence. The company wants a secure assistant that respects existing document permissions and needs no custom application development. Which service should it use?
x: Q Business is a fully managed enterprise assistant with built-in connectors (SharePoint, Confluence), and it honors user access permissions. Q Developer is for coding; Lex needs you to design intents.

q: A company runs a SageMaker real-time endpoint for a credit model. After six months, the approval rate for one age group has shifted significantly. The company wants automatic alerts when this kind of shift happens in the future. Which solution meets this requirement?
o: Enable SageMaker Model Monitor with SageMaker Clarify bias drift monitoring and CloudWatch alarms
Retrain the model every week without monitoring
Use AWS Config rules on the endpoint
Turn on Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging
x: Model Monitor integrates with Clarify to compute bias metrics on live traffic and alert through CloudWatch when they drift past thresholds. Config checks resource settings, not model behavior.

q: A data science team trains models in SageMaker. Security policy states that training data must never traverse the public internet and training containers must not make outbound calls. Which configuration meets these requirements?
o: Run training jobs in a private VPC with network isolation enabled and use VPC endpoints for S3
Use a public subnet with a NAT gateway
Encrypt the data with AWS KMS only
x: Network isolation blocks outbound calls from training containers, and VPC endpoints keep S3 traffic on the AWS network. KMS protects data at rest but doesn't control network paths.

q: A company must give auditors evidence that its generative AI workloads follow AWS best practices, and it wants that evidence collected continuously rather than manually before each audit. Which service should it use?
x: Audit Manager continuously gathers evidence from your accounts and maps it to frameworks, including a generative AI best-practices framework. Artifact only provides AWS's own compliance reports.

q: A company stores customer support transcripts in Amazon S3 and plans to use them to fine-tune a model. The security team must first identify which objects contain names, addresses and credit card numbers. Which service meets this requirement with the LEAST effort?
x: Macie automatically discovers and classifies sensitive data (PII, financial data) in S3 buckets. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, Config tracks configuration, and GuardDuty detects threats.

q: A security team needs to know which IAM user attempted to invoke an Amazon Bedrock model yesterday and was denied. Where can they find this information?
x: CloudTrail records every API call, including AccessDenied attempts, with the caller's identity. Invocation logs capture prompt and response content for successful invocations.

q: A company is fine-tuning a model in Amazon Bedrock and must encrypt the resulting custom model with keys it controls and can rotate or revoke. What should it do?
o: Use a customer managed key in AWS KMS when creating the customization job
Rely on Amazon S3 server-side encryption with S3 managed keys only
Store the model in AWS Artifact
x: Bedrock supports customer managed KMS keys for custom models and job data, giving you control over rotation, policies and revocation.

q: Which TWO tasks are the customer's responsibility when using Amazon Bedrock? (Choose TWO.)
o: Configuring IAM policies that control who can invoke models
Choosing what data is sent in prompts and protecting it
Patching the servers that host the foundation models
Maintaining the model providers' training pipelines
x: Under shared responsibility, AWS secures the infrastructure and managed service. Customers secure access (IAM), their data, configurations and how they use model outputs.

q: A government agency in Germany must keep all prompts and model outputs within the EU. It plans to use Amazon Bedrock. What should it consider?
o: Use Bedrock in an EU Region and restrict cross-Region inference to EU Regions only
Use any Region because Bedrock always processes data in the US
Enable Amazon CloudFront for low latency
x: Data residency follows the Region you use. Cross-Region inference profiles can route requests to other Regions, so choose EU-scoped profiles or disable cross-Region routing.

q: A hiring platform's model ranks candidates. An audit finds that candidates from one university are consistently ranked lower, even when qualifications are equal. Which TWO actions address this issue? (Choose TWO.)
o: Use SageMaker Clarify to measure bias metrics across groups
Rebalance or augment the training data so groups are fairly represented
Increase the number of training epochs
Remove model monitoring to reduce latency
x: Measure bias with Clarify, then fix the root cause with representative, balanced data. More epochs or temperature don't address fairness.

q: A medical imaging startup must explain to doctors why its deep learning model flags a scan as high-risk, and must document the model's limitations for regulators. Which combination of SageMaker features meets these requirements?
o: SageMaker Clarify for explanations and SageMaker Model Cards for documentation
SageMaker Ground Truth and SageMaker Canvas
SageMaker Feature Store and SageMaker Pipelines
SageMaker Data Wrangler and SageMaker Debugger
x: Clarify provides feature attributions (explainability); Model Cards document intended use, risks and evaluation for governance.

q: A company's generative AI marketing assistant sometimes produces images that closely resemble copyrighted characters. Which risk does this represent, and what is an appropriate mitigation?
o: Intellectual property infringement; add human review and content filters before publication
x: Output resembling protected works is an IP and copyright risk. Mitigate with review processes, filters, model choice and indemnified providers.

q: Users report that a chatbot confidently states incorrect product specifications that are not in the product catalog provided as context. Which Amazon Bedrock Guardrails feature directly detects this behavior?
x: Contextual grounding checks score whether a response is grounded in the provided source and relevant to the query, filtering hallucinations.

q: A company publishes a page explaining that its support chat is AI-powered, which data the AI uses, and how customers can reach a human. Which TWO responsible AI dimensions does this support? (Choose TWO.)
x: Disclosure supports transparency. Offering a path to a human and the ability to steer outcomes supports controllability and human oversight.

q: A manufacturer has years of sensor readings from machines but very few recorded failures. It wants to identify machines behaving unusually before they fail. Which ML approach is MOST suitable?
o: Supervised multi-class classification on failure labels
x: With few labeled failures, anomaly detection learns normal behavior from unlabeled data and flags deviations (e.g. the Random Cut Forest algorithm).

q: A model that predicts whether a patient has a rare disease shows 98% accuracy, but it misses most actual disease cases. Which metric should the team focus on improving?
x: Missing actual positives = false negatives, so improve recall. Accuracy is misleading with a rare class, and R² is for regression.

q: A data science team's model reaches 99% accuracy on training data but 70% on validation data. Which TWO actions are MOST likely to help? (Choose TWO.)
x: This is overfitting. More data and regularization or early stopping improve generalization. More epochs or complexity make overfitting worse.

q: A company needs predictions from an ML model for 10 million records every night. No one waits for the results in real time. Which SageMaker inference option is MOST cost-effective?
x: Batch transform scores whole datasets offline and shuts down afterward, with no persistent endpoint to pay for.

q: An app calls a fraud model only a few hundred times per day at unpredictable moments. The company wants to pay nothing when the model is idle and tolerates occasional cold-start delays. Which SageMaker inference option fits BEST?
o: Real-time inference on a GPU instance
x: Serverless inference scales to zero and bills per use, ideal for intermittent traffic where cold starts are acceptable.

q: A company's marketing analysts, who don't write code, want to predict which customers will churn using a CSV export from their CRM. Which solution requires the LEAST effort?
o: Amazon SageMaker Studio notebooks with XGBoost
x: Canvas is a no-code ML tool for business analysts: upload a CSV, pick the target column, build and predict.

q: A company needs a model that predicts next month's sales revenue for each store. Which type of ML problem and evaluation metric are appropriate?
x: Revenue is a continuous number, so this is regression. RMSE or MAE are the right metrics.

q: A team wants to classify customer emails into 12 complaint categories using its own labeled examples, without building ML models from scratch. Which service is MOST appropriate?
x: Comprehend custom classification trains a text classifier on your labeled examples with no ML expertise needed. Rekognition Custom Labels is for images.

q: A developer uses the same prompt to generate a legal disclaimer and receives different wording each time. The company needs consistent, repeatable output. Which change should the developer make?
x: Low temperature makes the model pick the most likely tokens, so output is near-deterministic. Higher Top P increases variety.

q: A company's prompts include long policy documents, and requests fail with an error saying the input is too long for the selected model. What are the BEST options? (Choose TWO.)
o: Choose a model with a larger context window
Use RAG to retrieve only the relevant chunks instead of whole documents
x: The input exceeds the context window. Either use a model with a bigger window or send only relevant chunks through retrieval.

q: A company wants semantic search across product photos and descriptions so that a customer can type 'red waterproof hiking boots' and find matching images. Which model type should power the index?
o: A multimodal embeddings model such as Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings
x: Multimodal embeddings map text and images into the same vector space, so text queries can retrieve similar images.

q: An AI practitioner must explain the difference between a large language model's 'tokens' and 'embeddings' to stakeholders. Which statement is correct?
o: Tokens are the units of text the model processes; embeddings are numeric vectors that represent the meaning of tokens or text
Tokens are numeric vectors; embeddings are words
Tokens are the model's weights; embeddings are its prompts
Tokens and embeddings are the same thing
x: Text is split into tokens (sub-word units), and each token or passage is represented as an embedding vector that captures meaning.

q: A mobile game company wants to run a language model directly on players' phones, with no internet connection required and minimal latency. What should it use?
o: A small, optimized language model deployed on the device
A large LLM accessed through the Bedrock API
x: On-device, offline, low-latency requirements call for small optimized models at the edge. Cloud APIs need connectivity and add network latency.

q: Which statement BEST describes how a diffusion model generates an image?
o: It starts from random noise and iteratively removes noise, guided by the text prompt, until an image emerges
It retrieves the closest stored image from a database
It uses a discriminator to reject unrealistic images during inference
It predicts the next word in a caption
x: Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noising process; at inference they denoise step by step conditioned on the prompt. GANs use discriminators.

q: A customer support team wants an LLM to classify tickets into 'billing', 'technical' or 'account' without any training. The LLM sometimes returns other labels. Which prompt technique MOST improves consistency?
o: Few-shot prompting with labeled example tickets and an explicit list of allowed labels
Zero-shot prompting with a higher temperature
x: Showing examples and constraining the output to an allowed list (few-shot plus clear instructions) gives consistent classification without training.

q: A financial analyst uses an LLM to solve multi-step calculations from earnings reports, and the model often skips steps and makes arithmetic errors. Which technique should the analyst try first?
o: Chain-of-thought prompting that asks the model to reason step by step
x: Chain-of-thought prompting improves multi-step reasoning by having the model show its intermediate steps, with no training needed.

q: Order the following options for adding company knowledge to an FM from FASTEST/CHEAPEST to implement to SLOWEST/MOST EXPENSIVE.
items: Put the relevant facts directly in the prompt (in-context learning)
Retrieval Augmented Generation with a knowledge base
Continued pre-training on a large domain corpus
x: In-context < RAG < fine-tuning < continued pre-training, in both cost and effort. Pick the cheapest one that meets the requirement.

q: A company measures its new gen-AI shopping assistant. Match each business question to the metric that answers it.
pairs: Does the assistant turn chats into purchases?
Does it reduce human agent workload?
x: Tie gen-AI to business outcomes: conversion (revenue), CSAT (experience), deflection (cost), latency (efficiency).

q: A company built a RAG application with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. Users complain that answers miss information buried in very long documents. Which change is MOST likely to improve retrieval quality?
o: Adjust the chunking strategy (chunk size and overlap) and re-sync the data source
x: Retrieval quality depends heavily on chunking. Better-sized, overlapping chunks (or hierarchical or semantic chunking) surface the right passages.

q: Match each customization goal to the BEST approach.
pairs: Answer from documents that change weekly
Always respond in a strict brand style and format
Learn a new domain's vocabulary from unlabeled text
Quickly steer a model for a one-off task
x: Fresh facts → RAG; behavior and style → fine-tuning with labeled pairs; domain knowledge from unlabeled data → continued pre-training; quick steering → prompts.

q: Match each Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix scope to an example.
pairs: Employees use a public gen-AI chat website
Using a SaaS CRM with built-in gen-AI features
Building an app that calls a Bedrock FM API
Fine-tuning a Bedrock FM with company data
Training a model from scratch on owned data
x: Ownership and security responsibility increase from Scope 1 to Scope 5.

q: Match each SageMaker capability to the problem it solves.
pairs: Need to clean and transform data visually
Need consistent features shared across teams
Need alerts when production data drifts
Need versioning and approval of models
x: Walk the ML lifecycle: label → prepare → features → train/explain → register → monitor.
